scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Strip the Willow is a Scottish ceilidh dance documented through early music transcriptions dating back to the 18th century, notably in David Young's 1734 manuscript and later in Francis O'Neill's 1907 collection.
on_screen: Map: Scotland · Europe
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Performed at ceilidhs, weddings, and social gatherings as an inclusive, high-energy group celebration.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers form longways sets of partners facing each other.
The top couple spins for 16 beats, then the lady strips down the line alternating left-hand turns with opposing men and right-hand turns with her partner.
The gentleman repeats the process up the line of ladies, followed by both stripping down the line together.
Watch for The Willow Strip.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Longways set facing partner across a parallel aisle

scenes.title: Welcome
narration: Chapter 1 — First steps. Today: Master partner elbow spin for 16 counts.
Level: Basic. Difficulty of the dance overall: beginner.
Your instructor: Warm, energetic Scottish ceilidh caller focused on social fun and clear counting
on_screen: Instructor front view, name of the chapter, the three things you will learn

scenes.title: Body and posture
narration: Upright, active social dance stance with flexible knees and firm elbow connections
Linked elbows (left arm to outside line, right arm to partner)
Torso rotates smoothly to absorb momentum of continuous turning
on_screen: Instructor front then side view; freeze-frame on validated posture

scenes.title: Count and rhythm
narration: Count: count the 9/8 or 6/8 bar out loud, then in pairs of bars. The meter is 9/8 or 6/8.
Rhythm pattern: Continuous driving compound jig pulse.
Clap it first, then step it in place.
on_screen: Counts on screen, flashing on the beat
Metronome at 84 bpm

scenes.title: Step A — slowly
narration: Step 1: Top couple link right arms and spin in the center for 16 beats.
Step 2: Lady turns line dancer anti-clockwise with left arm, then partner clockwise with right arm.

on_screen: Instructor front view, then back view (student's perspective); repetitions per step: about 4

scenes.title: Step B — the next layer
